business_scope.primary_industry_name: Computerized Embroidery and Ultrasonic Seaming of Custom Plush Dolls

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Colombia (unitary national jurisdiction, no sub-state corporate tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified Civil Code, Code of Commerce; S.A.S. governed by Law 1258 of 2008)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Colombia–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (in force May 15, 2012) – investment and dispute resolution chapter
Colombia–European Union Multilateral Trade Agreement (provisionally in force 2013, fully ratified 2021) – investment protection provisions
Canada–Colombia Free Trade Agreement (in force August 15, 2011) – investment chapter
Colombia–Switzerland Bilateral Investment Treaty (in force August 1, 2009)
Colombia–Spain Bilateral Investment Treaty (in force September 22, 2007)
Colombia–United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement (in force January 1, 2021), replicating EU investment commitments

DTAAs in force with Spain, Mexico, Chile, Canada, France, Germany, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, Portugal, South Korea, Japan, Switzerland and Brazil (select per residence of the foreign shareholder)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 526 of 1999 (creating UIAF, the Colombian Financial Intelligence Unit); Law 1121 of 2006 (terrorist-financing offenses); Law 599 of 2000, Articles 323 et seq. (money-laundering offense); Law 2195 of 2022 (anti-corruption); Decree 830 of 2021 and Superintendencia de Sociedades External Circular 005 of 2021 (SAGRILAFT AML/CFT/FPADM manual for the real sector); Decree 1023 of 2022 and DIAN Resolution 164 of 2021 (definition of Beneficiario Final and the annual Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales – RUBF filing obligation); Superintendencia Financiera AML rules applicable to Swift_TT and Platform_Pay payment rails.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access – the RUBF (DIAN) register is not public; accessible to DIAN, UIAF, Fiscalía General de la Nación, and authorized judicial/administrative supervisors only.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Extract of Registry of each corporate shareholder (Certificado de Existencia del Inversionista)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization if origin is not an Apostille state)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Special, sufficient and exclusive Power of Attorney (Poder Especial, Amplio y Suficiente) granted to a Colombian attorney-in-fact for the incorporation and registration acts
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the shareholder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of the passport of each non-resident shareholder, director and legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority or competent notary in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn Spanish translation (traducción oficial) of all apostilled foreign documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified official translator in Colombia (traductor oficial) or Colombian consular translation service
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No separate authentication – attach translation to the apostilled bundles and ratify before a Notaría Pública

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all incorporators, shareholders, directors, legal representatives and authorized signatories against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Colombian national risk lists (UIAF circulars; PEP lists maintained by the Presidential Council for Human Rights and SIGEP). PEP status is high-risk by default; source of funds and source of wealth declarations and senior compliance officer approval are mandatory for PEP shareholders. Adoption of a risk-based SAGRILAFT manual is recommended even though the mandatory asset/income threshold of COP 30,000 million is not met. Suspicious transaction reports (ROS) must be filed with UIAF within 10 business days. Enhanced due diligence applies where any shareholder holds 5% or more of capital or voting rights. Ongoing transaction monitoring applies to Swift_TT and Platform_Pay rails at account opening and during the operational life of the S.A.S.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) – https://www.rues.org.co, operated via the local Cámara de Comercio (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá for the Bogotá D.C. registered office).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be submitted in Spanish or in Latin-alphabet transliteration; accented Spanish characters and the letter 'ñ' are permitted; non-Latin scripts (e.g., Chinese characters, Cyrillic) are rejected and must be phonetically transliterated into Latin characters; the compulsory suffix 'S.A.S.' must appear in the definitive name as registered.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banco, Central de Inversión, Caja de Ahorros, Fondos de Pensiones, Fondo de Cesantías, Fondo de Inversión, Casa de Bolsa, Bolsa de Valores, Casa de Cambio – require prior authorization of the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia
Seguros, Reaseguros, Corredor de Seguros, Cooperativa de Seguros – require insurance sector licensing
Cooperativa, Mutual, Precooperativa – reserved for the cooperative legal form supervised by Superintendencia de la Economía Solidaria
Fundación, Corporación, Asociación – reserved for non-profit legal forms
Nacional, Presidencial, Oficial, Gobierno, Banco Central, Banco de la República – imply state affiliation and require ministerial approval
Cruz Roja, Media Luna Roja – protected emblems under international humanitarian law
Policía, Ejército, Fuerzas Militares, Defensa Civil – protected official denominations
Petróleos, Oleoducto, Minas, Energía Eléctrica – sector-specific terms requiring prior approval of the Ministry of Mines and Energy
Universidad, Colegio, Escuela – require Ministry of Education authorization
Clínica, Hospital, Laboratorio Clínico – require Ministry of Health administrative license

Any name identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company, trademark, or internationally known trade name – rejected by the Chamber of Commerce and Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The name reservation (Certificado de Homonimia) is automatically issued upon online filing through RUES and remains valid for 30 calendar days; a single extension of 30 additional days may be requested before expiration. On rejection, the applicant may either file a new name variant immediately through RUES, or file a reconsideration appeal (recurso de reposición) with the same Cámara de Comercio within 10 business days of notification. If denied, a hierarchical appeal (recurso de apelación) may be lodged with the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio within 10 business days; the SIC must decide within 30 business days. Incorporation must be completed within the reservation window or the reservation lapses.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted as the sole registered premise for a manufacturing business. The S.A.S. must state a real principal domicile (domicilio principal) in its bylaws; a virtual office may be used only as an administrative secondary address, provided a verifiable physical production facility exists for the plush-toy manufacturing activity. Registration with a virtual-only address exposes the company to registry refusal, bank account denial, and administrative sanctions.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-heightened risk: 35%–40% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months of operation. Inspections may be conducted by DIAN (tax substance verification), the Cámara de Comercio (address verification visits), municipal industrial safety and fire bureaus, and the Ministry of Labor. Textile manufacturing with stocked inventory increases the probability of municipal code enforcement visits.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cámara de Comercio (local chamber of commerce)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory chamber tariff applicable to the registered capital; typical range COP 30,000–50,000 (USD 8–13)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal drafting of S.A.S. bylaws (estatutos), private incorporation document, and registration checklist
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for standard S.A.S. incorporation files; COP 1.5–2.5 million (USD 400–650)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of signatures of the incorporators / attorney-in-fact before a Notaría Pública
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff per Superintendencia de Notariado y Registro; typical COP 60,000–120,000 (USD 16–32)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial registration of the S.A.S. in the Registro Mercantil and RUES enrollment
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration tariff calculated on declared capital; typical COP 90,000–200,000 (USD 24–54)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of official corporate books (libros oficiales) if prepared at incorporation stage
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per volume of books; optional until operations commence

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostilles for foreign shareholder documents (2–4 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authority for apostilles in the country of origin

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn Spanish translation of apostilled foreign documents (traducción oficial)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate per page, typically USD 20–30 per page for corporate and notarial documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Free of charge, mandatory statutory registration

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial UBO filing (RUBF – Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales) with DIAN

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial bank account opening compliance package (KYC/AML documentation, legal support)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial bank (e.g., Bancolombia, Davivienda) and corporate counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for AML/KYC onboarding support; bank internal fees may be waived

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Sociedades por Acciones Simplificadas), arts. 1, 3, 5, 18, 22 and 45; Código de Comercio (Decreto 410 de 1971), arts. 110-116 and 353-356; Decreto Único Reglamentario 1074 de 2015, Book 2.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (Registro Mercantil) and Notaría Pública; oversight by Superintendencia de Sociedades.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Private S.A.S. incorporation instrument (documento privado de constitución) with notarized signatures, or public deed (escritura pública) if real property is contributed; filed in the Registro Mercantil within 30 days.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is imposed on an S.A.S.; it may be formed with zero paid capital. Subscribed but unpaid capital can be paid under the statutory deferred-payment plan, and no escrow or blocked bank account is required by Colombian law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation instrument dated [DATE] is ratified and the authorized, subscribed, and paid capital stated in the bylaws is accepted; each subscriber's share subscription set out in Schedule A is approved and the shareholders' ledger ordered opened. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the company is [ADDRESS], and the legal representative is instructed to take possession of the premises and secure all municipal permits. RESOLVED, that [NAME] is appointed President and legal representative and [NAME] as Secretary, with all powers in the statutes, and is authorized to execute registration filings and bank account forms.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Availability and Homonymy Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (online homonymy search and name availability service)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three proposed corporate names to the Chamber's online 'consulta de homonimia' module. Verify that each name does not coincide or cause confusion with an existing registered company or protected trademark in the same registry; obtain the name availability certificate. This is a preliminary formality only and does not reserve the name indefinitely.
required_dossiers: full identification data of each subscriber and shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber identifies a conflict, submit an administrative opposition or select another proposed name and immediately re-run the availability check. A rejected certificate can be cured by amending the corporate name and re-submitting the same application form.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarial Authentication of the S.A.S. Incorporation Instrument
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública at the corporate domicile (notarial authentication desk)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the definitive private incorporation instrument and statutory bylaws. The document must contain the exact identification of shareholders, corporate name, domicile, corporate purpose, capital structure, duration, board or director provisions, and registered office. Take the signed document to the notary for authentication of signatures and content. If any shareholder contributes real property, the incorporation must be executed as a public deed before the same notary.
required_dossiers: signed bylaws executed by all shareholders
RUT of shareholders if previously registered
appraisal or title documents for in-kind contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The notary's objection may be resolved by correcting the instrument and re-authenticating. If the notary refuses due to doubts on legality, address the petition to the Superintendencia de Notariado y Registro or execute before another notary after validating the documentation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) – official portal: www.dian.gov.co; electronic services via MUISCA and RUTWeb.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must appoint a resident legal representative in Colombia, register with the local Chamber of Commerce (Cámara de Comercio) if forming a local branch or company, and obtain a tax identification number (NIT – Número de Identificación Tributaria) through DIAN. For a Colombian SAS, the incorporation process at the notary and Chamber of Commerce is followed by RUT (Registro Único Tributario) registration before DIAN to activate all tax obligations, including VAT (IVA) status as a responsible economic operator. A non-resident entity with Venezuelan-type activity must directly register with DIAN to obtain a NIT and VAT ID before issuing invoices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists under Colombian domestic law. The SAS may elect to be subject to the SIMPLE (Simplified Taxation Regime) if annual gross income is below the legal threshold (currently approximately COP 80,000,000), which replaces income tax and VAT for eligible small entities. Hybrid mismatch limitations and anti-deferral rules under Law 1955 of 2019 apply mandatorily; no elective regime is available to disregard the Colombian entity for tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA – Impuesto Sobre las Ventas (Colombia’s value added tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general registration threshold: all persons performing taxable activities in Colombia (sale of goods or provision of services) must register for IVA in the RUT, irrespective of turnover level. For services rendered by non-residents to Colombian recipients, the Colombian importer or recipient is the withholding agent and must self-assess IVA where the service is used in the national territory. Optional SIMPLE regime registration threshold: gross annual income below COP 80,000,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing (factura electrónica) operates through DIAN’s real-time validation system. Sellers must issue XML invoices with CUFE (Código Único de Facturación Electrónica) or CUDE (Código Único de Documento de Equivalencia) digital stamping, transmit each invoice to DIAN before delivery, and use only a DIAN-authorized technological provider (proveedor tecnológico). Fiscal clearance is real-time: no invoice is valid unless validated and electronically stamped by DIAN.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods from Colombian customs territory are zero-rated (0% IVA) and exempt from VAT on the final sale. Export of services and intellectual property may also qualify for zero-rating when the service is performed inside Colombia and economically used outside the country, provided the exporter meets DIAN’s documentary requirements and receives payment from abroad through authorized channels.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Declaration (Formulario de Exportación / Declaración de Exportación) mastered via MUISCA
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (Transport Document evidencing exit from Colombian customs territory)
Inward Remittance Certificate / Foreign Exchange Declaration (Certificación de Reintegro de Divisas o Declaración de Cambio)
Purchase Order, Sales Contract, and/or Manufacturing Service Agreement with foreign buyer
Customs Phytosanitary or Quality Certificates, if applicable, under DIAN and ICA requirements
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN may audit exporters retrospectively for up to five tax years. Fraudulent zero-rating claims trigger clawback of the full VAT benefit plus default interest, a penalty equivalent to up to 200% of the omitted tax (Article 675-2 and 697 of the Colombian Tax Statute), and criminal sanctions for customs fraud and illegal external trade operations. Exporters must retain the complete efflux, transport, and repatriation evidence for audit; failure to repatriate foreign currency within the 180-day deadline invalidates the zero-rating and exposes the exporter to immediate VAT assessment and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia, assisted by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia for bank and AML/CFT supervision and by the Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales for foreign-trade and customs reporting. The foreign-exchange policy is implemented through authorized intermediaries of the exchange market (intermediarios del mercado cambiario), principally local commercial banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia operates a managed-floating peso exchange-rate system with liberal but channeled convertibility. Current-account items — trade in goods, services, dividends, royalties, interest on registered financings, and other transfer payments — are freely convertible at the market exchange rate, provided they are routed through an authorized exchange intermediary when a foreign-currency payment or collection is involved. Capital-account transactions are permitted but subject to registration and intermediation rules: foreign direct investment in a Colombian S.A.S. must be registered with Banco de la República through the IMC using Form 5 (declaración de inversión internacional) in order for the investor to access the organized FX market for subsequent capital repatriation or profit remittance. Profit remittance is legally viable once the investee company has complied with annual corporate income-tax obligations, adopted dividend distributions at a shareholders meeting, supported the distribution with audited or legally sufficient financial statements, and paid the applicable dividend withholding tax. The main practical hurdles are documentary: delayed recognition of foreign investment, inconsistencies between the shareholder registry and the Form 5 filing, lack of transfer-pricing documentation for related-party transactions, and failure to maintain the exchange declaration with the IMC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For exports of tangible goods, the exporter must channel the corresponding foreign-currency proceeds through an authorized exchange intermediary and sell the proceeds in the Colombian exchange market within six months from the date of shipment, as evidenced by the transport document, unless Banco de la República has granted a special extension or the exporter is covered by a specific regime such as Free Trade Zones. The compulsory surrender ratio is effectively 100% of the FOB value of the export, net only of authorized expenses such as freight, insurance, and commissions that are paid through the exchange market and supported by proper documentation. The IMC issues an exchange declaration (declaración de cambio) evidencing the liquidation, and this declaration must be aligned with DIAN export declarations and the commercial contract for the plush toy OEM operations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account in Colombian pesos plus USD corporate deposit account for trade settlements
Operational Account in COP and foreign-currency transaction account
Operational Account / Foreign Investment Escrow Account overlay
Corporate Operational Account with trade and cash-management services
Operational Account linked to foreign trade and FX forward operations

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low as a primary banking channel and Medium as an ancillary digital payments component. An offshore digital EMI cannot replace a Colombian authorized exchange intermediary because Colombia mandates that export proceeds, foreign investment, and trade payments be channeled through the regulated exchange market. An overseas EMI wallet may be used as a supplementary collection/disbursement rail only if the competing foreign account is reported as a compensation account when required by Banco de la República and if all mandatory FX liquidations are normalized through the local IMC.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, the local legal representative of the S.A.S. must appear physically before the bank’s compliance officers at account opening, or alternatively use the bank’s digital onboarding platform where remote biographical identification is accepted under Colombian AML rules. Foreign non-resident directors and beneficial owners are not always required to travel, but they must provide notarized and apostilled powers of attorney, valid passports, proof of address, tax-residence certificates, and a signed beneficial-ownership declaration. Several banks require a physical interview for the legal representative and at least one board-level shareholder, particularly while the AML file contains non-resident individuals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership chain involving offshore trusts, holding companies, or multi-layer S.A.S. structures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete corporate organigram from ultimate individual to the Colombian entity; apostilled certificates of incorporation and good standing; tax-residence certificates of all intermediate entities; a lawful-source-of-funds declaration authenticated before a notary; bank statements of the ultimate shareholder; audited financial statements or accountant-prepared statements; and a written explanation of the commercial purpose of each layer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Political Exposed Person is a shareholder, director, or legal representative
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Express PEP status declaration; occupational and employment history; independent references; source-of-wealth report from a law firm or auditor; recent tax returns; biographical documentation; and a transaction-risk explanation for the capital injection into the plush-textile OEM company.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Counterparty or supplier appears in sanctions, adverse media, or high-risk jurisdiction screening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully annotated sanctions/OFAC clear-screen report; trade contracts and pro-forma invoices showing genuine commercial substance; bill-of-lading and air-waybill evidence; customs declaration; final customer and end-user data for the stuffed-animal exports; and a compliance memorandum explaining the business rationale and absence of third-party currency intermediary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the public registry shareholders and the beneficial-ownership declaration
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated electronic shareholder ledger of the S.A.S.; notarized share-transfer agreements; board resolutions or minutes of the shareholders meeting; consent declarations of actual beneficial owners; passport and tax ID copies; and a written commitment to register any future transfer with the bank before executing treasury operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusually rapid or staged flows of equity contributions and cross-border supplier payments without invoice evidence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital-injection SWIFT receipts referencing the investment registration number; signed import purchase orders for fabrics, polyester fiber, polyethylene stuffing, plastic eyes, and sewing accessories; commercial invoices and pro-forma invoices; transport documents; custom broker receipts; and the exchange declaration issued by the IMC for each transaction.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The non-resident shareholder initiates a SWIFT MT103 wire from its own bank account to the Colombian IMC’s correspondent account, with the beneficiary being the Colombian S.A.S. and the reference field stating Capital Contribution, shareholder name, and Colombian NIT. The funds may arrive in USD, EUR, or other freely convertible currency; upon crediting, the IMC converts to COP at the representative market rate and requests the client to file the foreign-investment registration before any disposal or dividend payment. For compliance completeness, the bank must receive: the corporate resolution authorizing the share subscription or capital increase, a notarized certificate of existence and representation of the S.A.S., shareholder identification, proof of source of funds, and a draft Form 5 for the Banco de la República registration. Loan capital should be structured separately as a shareholder loan with a documented loan agreement, market-rate interest, and tax substance to avoid recharacterization as hidden equity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlement of imported raw materials and tooling for the plush doll production should be executed by SWIFT MT103 for smaller pre-agreed trade payments or by commercial documentary letters of credit for larger, recurring shipments. The Colombian IMC will release foreign currency only against a supporting exchange declaration and the underlying trade documentation: commercial invoice, packing list, transport document, import declaration filed through DIAN, and, where applicable, cargo insurance. Payments must match the beneficiary name and account of the supplier stated in the contract; any prepayment, advance payment, or third-party settlement structure may be treated as an atypical payment operation and delayed by anti-money-laundering controls. All trade payments are reported using the applicable Colombian exchange concept code for imports of goods.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore COP/USD delivery forward contracts with authorized commercial banks, requiring an underlying trade receivable or payable in foreign currency
USD/COP non-deliverable forwards settled in COP at the reference TRM, executed through a Colombian IMC or licensed offshore bank with counterparty risk controls
Cross-currency swaps between COP and USD for long-term operational liquidity or foreign-investment matching
OTC FX options and other plain-vanilla derivatives entered through authorized intermediaries, subject to documented hedging exposure and Banco de la República transaction reporting

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil (annual commercial registry renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the registered office jurisdiction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal carries a 10% surcharge on the registry fee; failure to renew for two consecutive years allows the Cámara to cancel the mercantile registration, triggering administrative strike-off and potential dissolution of the S.A.S.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Depósito de Estados Financieros Anuales (annual financial statements filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio / Superintendencia de Sociedades
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 March following the 31 December fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing is sanctioned by Superintendencia de Sociedades fines of up to 60 SMLMV (approx USD 30,000); persistent non-compliance can lead to administrative intervention or dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaración de Renta y Complementarios (annual corporate income tax return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN - Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year ending 31 December; filing between 9 September and 2 October of the following year (exact day determined by last two digits of NIT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of the income tax due, plus daily late payment interest (approx 1.5% per month); repeated failures trigger tax enforcement, asset seizure, and cancellation of the NIT but do not directly strike off the corporate register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Actualización Anual de Beneficiarios Finales (UBO annual confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 July of each year (annual update of the beneficial owner status)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late submission fines of up to COP 21,000,000 (approx USD 5,000) plus daily interest; continued failure may suspend the entity's tax registration or restrict operations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaración Municipal de Industria y Comercio (ICA annual return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipal tax authority of the entity's domicile (e.g., Secretaría Distrital de Hacienda in Bogotá)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally due in April of each year; Bogotá deadline for annual ICA (previous year) is mid-April; exact date published by district ordinance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Municipal fines and daily interest; persistent non-filing permits tax recaudación enforcement and administrative sanctions by the municipality, but not corporate strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory Revisor Fiscal appointment is required where either gross assets exceed 5,000 SMLMV (approx COP 7,118 million in 2025) or gross revenue exceeds 3,000 SMLMV (approx COP 4,271 million). Below these thresholds, audit is optional unless the articles of incorporation require it or the entity is a public-interest/holding company.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS/NIIF as adopted in Colombia (NIIF Group 2 SME for small and medium-sized S.A.S.; full NIIF for public-interest entities).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Apply DIAN Resolution 164/2021: identify and report all natural persons the ultimate beneficial owner(s) holding at least 10% equity or control, provide individual identification details, and update annually by 31 July. Any share transfer resulting in a UBO change must be reported within 30 days of the change in addition to updating the Register of Members.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Accionistas)
Register of Directors (Libro de Actas de Asamblea y de Registro de Directivos)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 - USD 8,000 per year for an IFRS SME review/compilation; USD 5,000 - USD 15,000 for full statutory audit with Revisor Fiscal

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 25% income tax deduction for qualifying investments in science, technology and innovation (CTeI); 100% VAT discount and additional income deduction for investments in fixed productive assets; 50% additional payroll deduction for new employees under 28 years; ZESE special territorial regimes may apply (0% corporate tax for five years, then reduced rate subject to requirements).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 110 – Declaración de Renta y Complementarios; mandatory electronic filing via DIAN Muisca portal (www.dian.gov.co) with a valid registered electronic signature.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar fiscal year ending 31 December, the return and consolidated tax payment are due between the 9th and 15th calendar day of September of the following fiscal year, according to a DIAN-instructioned schedule by the last two digits of the NIT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIT, razón social, exercise year, and standard CIIU code (3240 – Manufacture of toys) stated in the header block.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the full legal name and NIT as registered in Colombia; for a branch or agent, indicate the permanent establishment code if any.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ingresos brutos por actividad económica: total gross invoiced proceeds from manufacture and sale of plush mascots, stuffed animals, OEM contract manufacturing, and embroidery/ultrasonic seaming services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Colombian-source revenue even if paid by a foreign parent into an offshore account; Colombian-source income is determined under the territorial rules and must not be excluded solely because payment originates abroad.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deducción por inversiones en ciencia, tecnología e innovación (CTeI): up to 25% of qualifying investments in product design, prototyping, automated embroidery software, and ultrasonic sealing equipment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the investment is physically or economically located in Colombia and dedicated to the CIIU 3240 production line; retain evidence of DIAN-registered projects.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Pérdidas fiscales del período: net operating losses carried forward from previous years after applying the 25% annual offset cap and the 15-year general carryforward limitation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must align the loss-schedule with the Colombian venture’s books; losses unrelated to the Colombian business are not deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Renta líquida gravable: net taxable income after all allowed deductions, exempt income, and the CTeI deduction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the non-resident holds a permanent establishment in Colombia, separate the PE’s ordinary income and file a branch return following the same line logic.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tarifa general de renta (35%): impuesto básico de renta computed as renta líquida gravable multiplied by the statutory rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the full 35% domestic rate before treaty credits; reduced treaty rates affecting withholding on related services should not be reflected here unless a PE allocates income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Descuentos tributarios: tax credits such as VAT paid on capital goods, CTeI tax credit, and any excess withholding on bank interest or commercial receipts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credits are only available to the legal entity that incurred the expense; a foreign shareholder cannot claim credits against Colombian corporate tax through the company.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Saldo a pagar o saldo a favor: final amount of corporate income tax due after prepayments (anticipos) and credits; paid via DIAN-approved electronic recaudo.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any relevant foreign tax credit must be substantiated with certificate of tax residence and proof of local withholding; if no definitive payment is due, the shareholder can request an official advance-ruling confirmation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or payment: 5% monthly surcharge on the income tax shown as due, capped at 100% of the tax; if no tax is due, a fixed penalty of 0.5% of the greater of net equity or gross assets, capped at 1,000 UVT. False filings or inaccurate returns: inaccuracy penalty equal to 100%–160% of the understated tax, plus criminal action for fraud.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding when the dividend is paid from profits already taxed at the 35% corporate rate; 35% withholding when the dividend source is exempt or untaxed income, with appropriate credits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a double taxation agreement (DTA), the non-resident shareholder must: (i) obtain an official Certificate of Tax Residency (TRC) from its home tax administration; (ii) deliver a certified Spanish-language TRC plus a sworn beneficial-ownership declaration to the Colombian payer before or at the time of dividend distribution; (iii) instruct the payer to apply the reduced treaty rate (e.g., 5% or 7.5% depending on the treaty); (iv) if excess tax is withheld, file a refund petition with DIAN within the statutory two-year limitation period, that is executed solely by senior management appointed under the S.A.S. articles.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for intellectual property, industrial rights, trademarks, and know-how: statutory withholding 30%; DTA treaty rates generally range from 7.5% to 10%, subject to beneficial ownership and substance test. Debt interest: statutory withholding 15% for financial loans; treaty rates commonly 5%–10%; non-treaty interest on loans granted by related non-residents is treated at the 15% statutory rate unless reduced by a treaty.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory TP local-file/master-file requirement for taxpayers whose gross income in the prior tax year equals or exceeds COP 3,000 million, or whose gross assets equal or exceed COP 5,000 million (annually adjusted by DIAN).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not have a standalone Economic Substance Regulation (ESR), but the S.A.S. must demonstrate genuine operational substance—physical manufacturing premises, production staff, inventory, utility consumption, and real negotiation functions—to resist GAAR recharacterization (Art. 260-10 E.T.) and to preserve DTA benefits. Shell structures lacking employees, production assets, and decision-making activity are open to judicial piercing and denial of treaty relief.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating gross receipts from export sales or OEM contracts in the CIIU 3240 activity, using false purchase or transportation invoices, manipulating inventory to inflate cost of sales, or destroying accounting records in Colombia.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inaccuracy penalty of 100%–160% of the understated tax, plus interest; criminal tax evasion under Article 350 of the Colombian Criminal Code carries imprisonment of 4 to 9 years and a fine of up to 100,000 UVT (approx. COP 4,706 million).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns or knowingly conceal Colombian-source revenue face joint and several civil liability for the unpaid tax, travel bans (restricción de salida del país), and criminal indictment for aggravated tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Contracting as a plush-toy OEM with no factory, no functional staff, no inventory, or no procurement activity, while shifting profits to a related foreign distributor through artificial margins or intra-company contracts lacking commercial reality.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN recharacterization under the Colombian GAAR / anti-abuse rules; denial of transfer pricing benefits and treaty reduction; imposition of the 160% inaccuracy penalty; potential inclusion in the DIAN 'inexistent firms' blacklist and cross-border tax information exchange referrals.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate veil pierced under civil fraud doctrines; directors are personally liable for resulting tax deficiencies, must disgorge unjust enrichment, and may face 5–8 years imprisonment for fraudulent simulation (interposita persona).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving payments in cash or crypto through unlicensed 'Platform_Pay' aggregators in exchange for plush-toy exports, engaging in purely circular payment flows to shell foreign traders, or moving SWIFT TT proceeds to non-beneficial owners without commercial-backed contracts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Prosecution under Law 1762/2015 and Criminal Code Article 323 (money laundering): imprisonment of 10 to 20 years, fines of COP 6,700 to 1 million UVT, seizure of goods and assets, together with closure of commercial establishments and mandatory imprisonment without parole for organised crime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors acting as beneficial owners or compliance officers who knowingly fail to perform customer-due-diligence or who process suspicious transactions are personally chased for restitution, may be subject to travel bans and provisional detention, and face incarceration up to 20 years.
